title: Checkpoint: American Voices
objective: After this level you can connect American writers from Poe to Morrison into one story of a national literature finding its own voices.
summary: From Poe to Morrison, American writers built a national literature from their own speech, music and history, in conversation; Native and Black voices beyond the chapter carry it on.

cards.headline: Chapter 8 finale: how did America find its own voices?
cards.body: From Poe's review of Hawthorne in 1842 to Morrison's Beloved in 1987, American writers kept asking the same question: what does our own voice sound like? Here is the path, the conversation, and the voices still joining in.

events.label: Poe's review of Hawthorne: the single effect
Huckleberry Finn, in a boy's own voice

cards.headline: Writers talking to writers
cards.body: This literature grew as a conversation. Poe used a review of Hawthorne's tales to set out his theory of the single effect. Melville, inspired by Hawthorne, dedicated Moby-Dick to him. Langston Hughes named Walt Whitman among his main influences. Each voice in this chapter was partly an answer to another.

cards.headline: More voices, older and newer
cards.body: This chapter's list is a start, not a fence. Stories in America are far older than Poe: Level 5's Haudenosaunee Sky Woman, set on a great turtle's back, is one. Zitkála-Šá, a Yankton Dakota writer, recalled a boarding school cutting off her braids: "Then I lost my spirit." N. Scott Momaday, a Kiowa writer, won the Pulitzer Prize for House Made of Dawn (1969). And James Baldwin, born in Harlem in 1924, carried a boyhood preacher's cadences into Go Tell It on the Mountain (1953).

mascot.line: This connects: the Sky Woman story from Level 5 and Zitkála-Šá's school days are American literature too, spoken and written.

cards.headline: Chapter 8 complete
learned: How American writers turned their own speech, music and history into a national literature.
Why Poe built a tale toward one effect, and how Hawthorne made a scarlet letter change its meaning.
How Douglass, Whitman and Dickinson each claimed a voice on the page.
What Huckleberry Finn and Beloved ask readers to face about slavery and memory.

questions.prompt: American stories are far older than Poe. In the Haudenosaunee creation story, Sky Woman is set down _____.

options.label: on a mountain after a flood
options.rationale: That's closer to Utnapishtim or Noah.

questions.explanation: Birds caught Sky Woman and set her on the back of a great turtle, where the muskrat's earth grew into Turtle Island.

questions.prompt: Match each writer or story with what goes with it.

pairs.right: Go Tell It on the Mountain

questions.explanation: Zitkála-Šá wrote "Then I lost my spirit" about her braids. N. Scott Momaday wrote House Made of Dawn, James Baldwin wrote Go Tell It on the Mountain, and Sky Woman was set on a great turtle's back.

questions.prompt: What did Poe say every word of a tale should serve?

options.label: A moral stated at the end
A regular rhyme scheme
options.rationale: Poe was talking about prose tales.

options.label: As long a plot as possible

questions.explanation: Poe held that a writer first conceives a single effect, and every word should serve that one design.

questions.prompt: How was Nathaniel Hawthorne linked to both Poe and Melville?

options.label: Poe reviewed his tales; Melville dedicated Moby-Dick to him
He published both men's first books
He sailed with both of them on the whaleship Acushnet in 1841
He taught both of them at Harvard

questions.explanation: Poe set out his single-effect theory in a review of Hawthorne's tales, and Melville dedicated Moby-Dick to Hawthorne.

questions.prompt: Langston Hughes named one great 19th-century American poet among his main influences. Who?

options.label: Emily Dickinson
options.rationale: Not among the influences he named.

options.label: Edgar Allan Poe
options.rationale: Not among the influences he named.

questions.explanation: Hughes cited Paul Laurence Dunbar, Carl Sandburg and Walt Whitman as his primary influences.
